children: Saudi Aramco has invested almost 9.9 billion Saudi riyals ($2.6 billion)in cash this year in HUMAIN, the state-backed artificial intelligence (AI) company, which will monetise the oil giant’s existing AI and digital assets.
Aramco, through a wholly owned subsidiary, has acquired a 49 percent stake in HUMAIN, while the Public Investment Fund (PIF) retains 51 percent ownership, the comapny said in a joint statement.
The transaction will accelerate HUMAIN’s growth and advance its full range of AI capabilities globally, with PIF and Aramco contributing AI assets, capabilities, and talent.
Aramco is expected to leverage HUMAIN’s AI infrastructure to translate advanced AI capabilities into industrial applications, further enhancing its operations.
Launched in May 2025, HUMAIN is developing 3 gigawatts of AI data centre capacity by 2030.

This month, HUMAIN and DataVolt, a data centre infrastructure developer, signed a preliminary framework agreement with Nebius, an AI cloud company, for 50 megawatts (MW) of data center capacity at Oxagon in NEOM.
HUMAIN and DataVolt agreed in August to jointly develop 100 MW of a 360 MW AI-ready data center at Oxagon.
In the same month, HUMAIN awarded a contract to Saudi-listed Al Moammar Information Systems Company (MIS) to expand the capacity of its data centre from 50 MW to 250 MW.

title: Saudi Aramco takes a 49% stake in HUMAIN with $2.6bln investment
